body.estimand_functional: \(\widetilde U_C=(M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\overline W_z)_{k\in\mathcal K}\), with full covariance \(\Sigma_B^{(K)}\) under \(\mathsf B(p)\) and \(\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}\) under all-positive-share \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\).

sampling_model.design: Exactly one regime is active. In \(\mathsf B(p)\), labels are iid categorical and units are conditionally independent Bernoulli. In \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), the label vector has fixed counts \(C_{C,k}\) and each cluster is conditionally uniform on its exact-count slice.
sampling_model.units: Observe \(C\) independent equal-size cluster schedules from an unrestricted bounded \([0,1]\)-valued potential-outcome law, with no interference across clusters and arbitrary interference within a cluster.
sampling_model.treatment: The schedule law \(P\) is mapped to observed data by the known kernel \(R_{B,p}\) or the joint fixed-count kernel \(R^{CR}_{C_C}\); scores and influence functions live in the induced observed-law spaces.
sampling_model.overlap: Interior rational saturations make every Bernoulli hit rate positive. Active-face CR results require positive shares only on \(A\); the full-vector CR CLT and all-policy rank theorem require \(\alpha_k>0\) for every reported policy.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate assignment-specific means and variances within realized target cells, average cells uniformly within each exact-count slice, and use a prespecified bounded fallback for empty cells. Covariance-driven selection may use sample splitting.

body.tldr: The headline result prices the loss from using Bernoulli-label data to select the welfare-maximizing exact-count policy: on every declared tied-best face, the optimized best-policy simple-regret ratio is bounded by active exact-hit mass with an exact equality frontier, and the squared ratio gives the cluster-count penalty. Separate observed-law theorems establish finite-sample nuisance deletion, full-menu calibrated CLTs, active-face LAN lower experiments, and tie-valid rank inference. The closest same-target estimator is transcribed exactly from Han--Owusu--Shin Appendix-B Eq. (S1); its derived influence variance reveals cross-label, assignment-cell, and Horvitz--Thompson participation losses. For a non-symmetric three-policy menu, exact arithmetic reports the hit matrix, its column masses, and its unique maximum-mass normalized column; the general certified routine supplies optimizer and risk enclosures once a variance vector and tolerance are specified, but no executed numerical transcript is reported here. A screened hierarchical construction certifies the noncompact general-K game across retained partial-tie faces and uniformly positive-definite covariance cells, with explicit zero-rate boundary handling and full quotient-ball primitive transfer.

project_justification.gap: Same-target saturation-ranking work uses the nominal-label Horvitz--Thompson estimator in Appendix-B Eq. (S1) and a rule-specific regret envelope; it does not give all-rule nuisance deletion, observed-law target tangents, a sharp face-specific mechanism-deficiency frontier, or a validated noncompact Gaussian outer-design implementation.
project_justification.niche: Exact-count deployment exposes the known hit polytope \(B\Delta_K\) inside an unrestricted within-cluster interference model. Treating common welfare as a nuisance and passing both means and observations to their contrast quotient allows the assignment mechanism itself to be priced for the same causal target.
project_justification.fill: The project makes mechanism loss the sole headline, derives its observed-score and efficiency foundations, proves the exact Han variance comparison, and couples a Joo-informed Gaussian selector to calibrated cluster data. Its certified screened hierarchy handles unbounded contrasts by enumerating retained subfaces, transfers each full compact quotient ball through a surjective representative set, and certifies both outer allocation problems on their stated positive-rate domains.

body.related_work:
HanOwusuShin2026 is the closest same-estimand paper, but its decision action is a full vector of pairwise rankings under additive pairwise regret, whereas the headline mechanism game here selects one welfare-maximizing policy under simple regret. The nuisance-deletion theorem separately covers the published ranking action.

HanOwusuShin2026 is the closest same-target paper. Its Appendix-B Eq. (S1), pp. 40--44, uses the Horvitz--Thompson normalization \(1/(Cp_k)\) and a within-label likelihood ratio; the exact comparison theorem derives its influence variance and strictly refines it through cross-label assignment calibration. HiranoPorter2009 supplies the limit-experiment architecture, but the all-rule nuisance-deletion theorem and legal observed-law exact-hit tangent are specific to this model. BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018 makes saturation shares a design object under a power criterion rather than optimized facewise simple regret. Joo2025 informs the static Gaussian selector; the contribution here is its coupling to the exact-hit polytope, a general certified outer-design procedure over the exact-hit polytope, and calibrated cluster-data transfer, not a new generic Gaussian minimax construction. Kato2026, arXiv:2506.24007v6 dated 25 July 2026, is Masahiro Kato's adaptive sequential best-arm comparator and only informs the certification architecture. LoombaEckles2026 informs score projection under structured interference. JiangImaiMalani2023 and MogstadRomanoShaikhWilhelm2024 inform the supporting covariance and rank-inversion results. ChanNakamuraSakaiForastiere2023 is nonarchival prior use of cross-label information for a different hypothetical-allocation target. EggerHaushoferMiguelNiehausWalker2022 supplies the prospective Kenya saturation-design consumer.
body.interpretation: The causal object is the finite-population-style exact-slice welfare vector, while \(B\), \(q=Bp\), the calibrated estimator, and the Gaussian game are respectively design, observed-law, estimation, and decision functionals.  Their relationship is proved: exact hits supply information \(q_k/\tau_k^2\), calibration removes the between-assignment mean component, local asymptotic normality transfers the experiment to the translation-quotient Gaussian game, and the certified optimizer converts the resulting risk into a prospective allocation.  Thus the mechanism penalty is a loss of assignment information for the same causal target, not a change of estimand.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The noncompact routine is uniform over the finitely many retained subsets inside a declared face and over compact positive-definite covariance cells. Bernoulli hit positivity supplies the full outer-simplex transfer. Exact-count primitive transfer is restricted to compact positive-share allocation sets; at an action-relevant zero share only the proved extended value \(+\infty\) is asserted.
body.honest_scope: The results concern fixed \(n\), fixed \(K\), equal cluster sizes, distinct interior rational saturations, isolated iid cluster schedules, and exact-slice welfare. Bernoulli-label and exact-count complete randomization are mutually exclusive regimes, and all scores are defined under their induced observed laws. Active-face CR results allow zero inactive shares, but the full-menu CR CLT and rank theorem require every reported share to be positive. At a unique best policy first-order local regret is zero. When \(K=2\), the face game reduces to the classical sign rule and Neyman allocation; assignment-homogeneous slice means eliminate the calibration component but not necessarily the Horvitz--Thompson participation term in Eq. (S1). The finite positive-face Gaussian certificate is a theorem target; the three-policy calculation reports only exact hit-matrix and column-mass arithmetic, not an executed optimizer or risk certificate. The Kenya design is a prospective design consumer rather than an authorized reanalysis. For the Appendix-B Eq. (S1) comparator, the note matches the published equal-size, finite-interior-menu, iid-cluster, bounded-outcome, unrestricted within-cluster-interference class, while dropping unnecessary smoothness and allowing boundary nominal-label shares via cross-label hits. Han–Owusu–Shin’s broader main complete-randomization envelope also permits heterogeneous integral cluster sizes; the present equal-size converse transfers upward as a lower bound on that broader class, but the efficient upper construction, single hit map, and exact mechanism frontier are not claimed there.
